quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Full-time employees receive twenty-five days of paid holiday a year, rising to thirty after five years of service. Public holidays are additional. Up to five unused days may be carried into the next year; any beyond that are lost unless a manager approves an extension in writing. Staff may also buy up to three extra days through salary deduction, but this must be requested before the end of January. Part-time employees receive holiday in proportion to their hours, and new joiners receive days for the months remaining in the year. Requests of more than ten consecutive days need approval at least six weeks ahead.
quests.question: How many unused days can most employees carry forward automatically?
options: Three
Ten
Five
Thirty
quests.correctAnswer: Five
quests.hint: Numbers crowd this text. Match each one to its rule before choosing.
quests.explanation: Five days can be carried over without permission. Ten refers to consecutive days, three to purchased days and thirty to long service.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Runners training for a marathon are often told to drink as much as possible, but recent guidance is more cautious. Drinking too much can dilute the sodium in the blood, causing a dangerous condition called hyponatraemia, which is more common among slower runners who spend longer on the course and take every drink offered. The advice now is to drink when thirsty, and to add salt or an electrolyte drink in very long or hot events. Rather than following a fixed schedule, runners should learn how much they lose by weighing themselves before and after training runs. Coaches add that cool, humid weather can reduce sweating, so the risk exists even in races that do not feel hot.
quests.question: Why are slower runners more at risk of hyponatraemia?
options: They are on the course longer and drink at every station
They lose less sodium in their sweat than faster runners
They weigh themselves too often before races
They avoid electrolyte drinks completely
quests.correctAnswer: They are on the course longer and drink at every station
quests.hint: The explanation is in the same sentence as the condition. Pick out the two reasons it gives.
quests.explanation: Slower runners spend more time on the course and take every drink, so they consume more fluid than they lose. Weighing is presented as a solution, not a cause.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The council's budget for the coming year totals 420 million dollars, an increase of three percent. Education receives the largest share at 38 percent, followed by roads and transport at 17 percent and social care at 15 percent. The remaining funds cover housing, libraries, parks and administration. Council tax will rise by 2.5 percent, the smallest increase in six years, and the council says this can be achieved partly by delaying a new leisure centre until the following year. Opposition members argue that services are being cut and that the delay only postpones costs. The largest single project is a new bridge over the river, which will begin in September and cost 34 million dollars.
quests.question: How is the council keeping the tax rise small?
options: By charging more for parks and sports grounds
By reducing school funding by a few percent
By postponing construction of a leisure centre
By closing several libraries in the outer districts
quests.correctAnswer: By postponing construction of a leisure centre
quests.hint: Ignore the percentages for a moment and look for the action that explains the small increase.
quests.explanation: The text links the 2.5 percent rise to delaying the leisure centre. The other options are budget lines or claims made by the opposition, not the council's method.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: To be considered for the engineering programme, applicants must hold a secondary school certificate with at least a B average in mathematics and physics. Those who studied abroad must submit certified translations. Applications open on 1 November and close on 15 January, but candidates for the scholarship route must apply a month earlier. Interviews are held only for candidates whose grades fall just below the requirement or whose applications include unusual experience. Successful applicants receive an offer by the end of March and have until 30 April to accept. Deferred entry for one year is possible with the department's permission, but the place is not guaranteed for candidates who do not reply.
quests.question: By when must a scholarship-route candidate apply?
options: 30 April
1 November
15 December
15 January
quests.correctAnswer: 15 December
quests.hint: The deadline is described relative to another date. Do the subtraction.
quests.explanation: The general deadline is 15 January, and scholarship candidates apply a month earlier, on 15 December. The other dates are the opening of applications and the acceptance deadline.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Your itinerary has changed. Flight BX 410 from Manchester to Zurich now leaves at 10:35 rather than 08:50, arriving at 13:20 local time. Because of the later arrival, your connection to Vienna, originally at 11:30, has been moved to 15:45 at no cost. Your checked baggage will be transferred automatically, but you must collect your boarding pass for the second flight at the transfer desk in Terminal B. If the new arrival time in Vienna, 17:10, is not suitable, contact us before Friday to discuss alternatives. Meals are not included on either flight, and the airline will provide a voucher worth ten euros for the longer wait in Zurich.
quests.question: What must the passenger do in Zurich?
options: Contact the airline before Friday to change the flight
Change the connection back to 11:30 at no cost
Claim and re-check the baggage at the transfer desk
Collect a boarding pass at the transfer desk
quests.correctAnswer: Collect a boarding pass at the transfer desk
quests.hint: Separate what happens automatically from what the passenger must do personally.
quests.explanation: Baggage moves by itself, and the passenger's own task is to pick up the second boarding pass. Contacting the airline is only needed if the Vienna time is unsuitable.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Renewable sources supplied 42 percent of the country's electricity last year, up from 36 percent the year before, according to the energy regulator. Wind accounted for most of the increase, while solar power grew more slowly because of a wet summer. Gas remained the largest single source at 31 percent, but its share fell for the third year running. The regulator cautions that the figures may not reflect the whole grid, as small generators do not always report their output. Coal, which supplied 12 percent a decade ago, now provides almost nothing. Officials expect renewables to reach half of all supply within three years if planned wind farms are completed on time.
quests.question: What is the regulator's warning about the figures?
options: Solar output was recorded too high in the wet summer
Some small producers may be missing from them
Wind power was overestimated by the regulator
Gas use is rising again after three years of decline
quests.correctAnswer: Some small producers may be missing from them
quests.hint: A warning is signalled by a verb like "cautions". Read only that sentence.
quests.explanation: Small generators do not always report, so the figures may be incomplete. The other options twist facts from elsewhere in the passage.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The tenant agrees to pay rent of $950 on the first of each month by bank transfer. A deposit of $1,425, equal to six weeks' rent, is held in a protected scheme and will be returned within ten days of the tenancy ending, less any deductions for damage beyond normal wear. The tenant may keep a small pet with the landlord's written consent, provided an additional deposit of $150 is paid. Subletting is not permitted. Either party may end the agreement after the first six months by giving two months' written notice. The tenant is responsible for minor repairs costing under fifty dollars, while the landlord must arrange all structural work.
quests.question: What is required in order to keep a pet?
options: Two months' written notice to the landlord
Membership of the protected deposit scheme
An extra deposit only, with no consent needed
The landlord's written consent and an extra deposit
quests.correctAnswer: The landlord's written consent and an extra deposit
quests.hint: One sentence holds two conditions joined by "provided". Make sure your choice has both.
quests.explanation: A pet needs written consent and an additional $150 deposit. Choosing only one condition is the typical mistake.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The community health clinic offers free flu vaccinations to people aged sixty-five and over, pregnant women and anyone with a long-term condition such as asthma or diabetes. Appointments are available on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and walk-in sessions run on the first Saturday of the month. Please bring your health card and wear a short-sleeved top. Those who feel unwell with a fever should postpone their appointment. The vaccination takes about ten minutes, and you will be asked to wait fifteen minutes afterwards in case of any reaction. Parking is limited, so patients are encouraged to arrive on foot or by bus, and an interpreter can be arranged if requested a day earlier.
quests.question: Who should postpone their appointment?
options: People aged over sixty-five
People who have a fever
Pregnant women
People with asthma
quests.correctAnswer: People who have a fever
quests.hint: Three groups are eligible; only one situation is a reason to delay.
quests.explanation: Fever is the condition that calls for postponement. The other groups are those who qualify for the free vaccination.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Our menu marks vegetarian dishes with a green leaf and dishes containing nuts with a red dot. The lamb curry, $18, contains no nuts but is cooked with yoghurt, so it is not suitable for anyone avoiding dairy. The mushroom risotto, $15, is vegetarian and dairy-free if requested without cheese. The almond cake, $8, contains nuts, as does the vegetable stir-fry, $14, which is finished with cashew sauce. Please tell your server about any allergies before ordering, since dishes may be prepared in the same kitchen as nuts. Children's portions are available for all main dishes at two thirds of the price, and tap water is always free.
quests.question: Which dish suits a vegetarian who is allergic to nuts?
options: The lamb curry
The almond cake
The vegetable stir-fry
The mushroom risotto
quests.correctAnswer: The mushroom risotto
quests.hint: Cross out dishes one requirement at a time: first meat, then nuts.
quests.explanation: The lamb curry is not vegetarian, and the cake and stir-fry contain nuts. Only the risotto passes both tests.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: This warranty covers manufacturing defects for twenty-four months from the date of purchase. It does not cover damage caused by accidents, water, or repairs carried out by anyone other than an authorised centre. Batteries are covered for twelve months only. To make a claim, contact customer service with your receipt and the serial number, which is found under the battery. If the product cannot be repaired, it will be replaced with an equivalent model. Shipping costs are covered only for the first twelve months. Replacement models may be refurbished, and the new item carries only the remainder of the original warranty period.
quests.question: Which situation would be covered by the warranty?
options: A phone dropped in water in the third month
A battery failing after fourteen months
A screen fault appearing after eighteen months
A repair done by a friend in the sixth month
quests.correctAnswer: A screen fault appearing after eighteen months
quests.hint: Test each situation against the type of problem and the time limit.
quests.explanation: A manufacturing fault within twenty-four months is covered. Water damage, an unauthorised repair and a battery beyond twelve months are all excluded.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Registration for the city marathon closes on 1 September, and places are allocated by ballot if demand exceeds the 12,000 available. Runners who complete the race in under three hours qualify for a guaranteed place next year. The start is at 8:30 a.m. in Central Park, with runners placed in pens according to their expected finish time. Roads along the route close from 6 a.m., and public transport to the park runs every ten minutes from 5:30. Bags must be handed in by 8:00, and no supporters are allowed within the start area. Finishers receive a medal and a bottle of water, and a free massage is offered in the tent behind the finish line.
quests.question: How can a runner secure a place next year?
options: By registering before 1 September for the ballot
By arriving at the start before 8:00 a.m.
By starting the race in an early pen
By finishing this year's race in under three hours
quests.correctAnswer: By finishing this year's race in under three hours
quests.hint: Look for the word that promises something in the future.
quests.explanation: A guaranteed place goes to runners who finish in under three hours. The registration date and start pens are unrelated to next year's entry.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The museum offers three membership levels. Individual membership costs $60 a year and includes unlimited entry and a ten percent discount in the shop. The Family level, at $110, covers two adults and up to three children. The Patron level, at $250, adds invitations to private views and one guest pass per visit. All members receive the quarterly magazine, and memberships can be given as gifts. Students under twenty-five pay $40 for the individual level upon showing valid identification, but this cannot be combined with any other discount. Members who join in the last two months of the year receive an additional three months free.
quests.question: What does the Patron level include that the others do not?
options: A ten percent discount in the museum shop
Unlimited entry to the museum for a year
Invitations to private views and a guest pass
The quarterly magazine sent to all members
quests.correctAnswer: Invitations to private views and a guest pass
quests.hint: The word "adds" signals what is extra at the highest level.
quests.explanation: Only the Patron level offers private views and a guest pass. The magazine is for all members, and unlimited entry and a shop discount come with the individual level.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Progress on the library renovation is slightly behind schedule. The roof repairs were completed last month, but delivery of the new windows has been delayed by three weeks because of a shortage at the manufacturer. Electrical work is on track, and the plumbing inspection is due on the 12th. If the windows arrive by the 30th, the contractor believes the reopening date of 15 October can still be met, though painting would have to be done at weekends. The budget remains within limits, with 92 percent spent. A meeting with local residents will take place on the 20th to explain how noise from the work will be limited.
quests.question: What could threaten the reopening date?
options: A failure of the plumbing inspection on the 12th
Roof repairs that remain unfinished
A further delay in the delivery of the windows
Spending more than the budget allows this month
quests.correctAnswer: A further delay in the delivery of the windows
quests.hint: Find the condition on which the contractor's confidence depends.
quests.explanation: The 15 October date holds only if the windows arrive by the 30th. The roof is finished and the budget is within limits.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Self-employed workers must submit their tax returns by 31 January if they file online, or by 31 October of the previous year if they use paper forms. Payment is due on the same date as online filing, whichever method is used. Late filing brings an automatic fine of one hundred dollars, and additional charges apply after three months. Those who cannot pay in full should contact the tax office before the deadline to arrange an instalment plan, since doing so can avoid further penalties. Those who are employed as well as self-employed should include both incomes on the same return, and receipts must be kept for five years.
quests.question: What should someone who cannot pay in full do?
options: Pay the hundred dollar fine and delay the tax itself
Contact the tax office before the deadline
Wait for three months before contacting anyone
Switch to a paper form and file it early
quests.correctAnswer: Contact the tax office before the deadline
quests.hint: The advice is tied to a word of reason, "since", at the end.
quests.explanation: Arranging an instalment plan in advance can avoid further penalties. Paper forms have an earlier deadline, and waiting adds charges.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Camping is permitted only in designated areas of the national park, and reservations are required from May to September. Fires are allowed only in the metal rings provided, and firewood must be bought at the visitor centre because collecting wood from the forest damages habitats. Food must be stored in the lockers to keep bears and smaller animals away, and rubbish must be carried out. Quiet hours are from ten until seven. Groups larger than eight need a special permit, which can take two weeks to process. Pets must be kept on a lead at all times, and drones are not permitted anywhere in the park.
quests.question: Why must firewood be bought at the visitor centre?
options: The metal rings are too small for most tents
Fires are banned throughout the summer season
Bears are attracted to wood stored in the lockers
Gathering wood harms wildlife habitats
quests.correctAnswer: Gathering wood harms wildlife habitats
quests.hint: The reason follows the word "because", not the rule itself.
quests.explanation: Collecting wood in the forest damages habitats, which is why it must be bought. Bears are mentioned only in connection with food.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Parents must notify the school by 9 a.m. on the first day of any absence, by phone or through the school app. If no message is received, the school will send a text and, if there is still no reply by noon, call the emergency contact. Absences of more than three consecutive days require a doctor's note. Family holidays during term time are not authorised except in exceptional circumstances, and repeated unauthorised absence may lead to a meeting with the head teacher and, ultimately, a fine. Pupils who arrive after 8:45 must sign in at reception, and three late arrivals in a week count as one unauthorised absence.
quests.question: When is a doctor's note required?
options: For any absence at all, however short the time
When a pupil is away for more than three days in a row
For family holidays taken during the term
Whenever a parent forgets to call the school office
quests.correctAnswer: When a pupil is away for more than three days in a row
quests.hint: A number and a word for "in a row" define the trigger.
quests.explanation: Only absences longer than three consecutive days need a note. Forgotten calls lead to texts and phone calls, and holidays are a separate rule.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Customers whose broadband is down for more than forty-eight hours are entitled to automatic compensation of ten dollars per day after the second day. The fault must be reported to us, and compensation is not paid for problems caused by the customer's own equipment or by events such as storms that are outside our control. Payments appear as a credit on your next bill. If you have a business account, different terms apply, and you should contact your account manager for details. The compensation scheme does not apply during planned maintenance, which is always announced at least a week in advance.
quests.question: When is compensation NOT paid?
options: When the customer reports the fault straight away
When the credit shows up on the next bill
When the outage lasts three days or longer
When a storm beyond the company's control causes the fault
quests.correctAnswer: When a storm beyond the company's control causes the fault
quests.hint: Look for the exception clause; it contains two examples.
quests.explanation: Events outside the company's control, such as storms, are excluded. An outage lasting three days actually qualifies for payment.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Passengers may carry liquids in containers of no more than 100 millilitres in cabin baggage, provided that all containers fit into a single transparent bag of one litre. The bag must be presented separately at security. Exceptions are made for baby food, essential medicines and special dietary products, which may be carried in larger quantities if verified by security staff. Drinks bought after security are permitted, but duty-free liquids bought on connecting flights must be sealed in a special bag with the receipt visible. Passengers should also remove laptops and large electronic devices from their bags, as these are screened separately.
quests.question: Which item may exceed 100 ml in cabin baggage?
options: Perfume in a clear bag over the limit
Baby food, after checking by security staff
Shampoo for personal use in a large bottle
A bottle of water bought before the airport
quests.correctAnswer: Baby food, after checking by security staff
quests.hint: The word "Exceptions" opens the sentence that answers this.
quests.explanation: Baby food is on the exception list, provided staff verify it. Shampoo, water and perfume are ordinary liquids bound by the 100 ml rule.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A study of 1,800 university students compared outcomes in classes taught entirely online with those taught in person. Overall grades were similar, but students in online classes who had reliable internet and a quiet place to study performed better, while those without them performed worse. Attendance at live sessions was lower online, but students who watched recordings did as well as those who attended. The authors conclude that online teaching is not inherently worse and that the differences arise mainly from students' circumstances. The researchers add that universities should therefore lend equipment and provide study spaces before deciding which classes to move online.
quests.question: What do the authors conclude?
options: Recordings are worse than live classes for learning
Grades depend chiefly on how often students attend
Differences mostly reflect students' circumstances
Online teaching is always weaker than classroom teaching
quests.correctAnswer: Differences mostly reflect students' circumstances
quests.hint: The conclusion is usually signalled by a word such as "conclude".
quests.explanation: The authors attribute differences to conditions at home rather than to the teaching format. Recordings performed as well as live attendance.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Last year the supermarket cut its packaging by 12 percent, mainly by removing plastic wrapping from fruit and replacing plastic bags with paper. It also reduced food waste by a fifth, partly through discounting items close to their date. However, its total carbon emissions fell by only two percent, since more delivery vans were needed for the online service. The company says the next target is to make all delivery vehicles electric by 2030, and it admits that this depends on charging infrastructure. Meanwhile, the chain will trial refillable containers for laundry products in twenty stores, and customers will bring their own bottles.
quests.question: Why did carbon emissions fall by only two percent?
options: Packaging increased
More delivery vans were needed
Electric vehicles arrived late
Food waste rose
quests.correctAnswer: More delivery vans were needed
quests.hint: A contrast word introduces the disappointing figure; the reason follows "since".
quests.explanation: The online service required more vans, which offset gains elsewhere. Packaging and waste both went down.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Early registration for the conference costs $250 until 31 March, after which the standard fee of $320 applies. Students pay $120 regardless of date, but must upload proof of enrolment. Groups of five or more from the same organisation receive ten percent off the standard or early fee. The fee includes lunch and coffee on both days, but not the gala dinner, which is available for an additional $60. Cancellations are refunded in full until 1 May, and half after that. Sessions are recorded and available for three months, but recordings are not included in the student rate.
quests.question: How much does each member of a group pay if they register after 31 March?
quests.hint: Find the standard price first, then apply the group discount.
quests.explanation: Ten percent off $320 is $32, giving $288. The student price and the early fee do not apply.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Before setting off, tell someone your route and expected return time. Carry a map and compass even if you rely on a phone, since batteries fail in the cold and signal is unreliable in valleys. Turn back if the weather changes suddenly, as conditions on the ridge can worsen within an hour. If you become lost, stay where you are rather than wandering, and use a whistle to signal: six blasts in a minute, repeated after a minute's pause. Searchers are more likely to find a stationary group. In winter, carry a spare layer and a high-energy snack, and never drink water from streams without treating it.
quests.question: Why should a lost hiker stay put?
options: Rescuers are more likely to find someone who is not moving
Walking makes the whistle sound quieter to searchers
The weather improves in valleys where people wait
Phones work better when the user is standing still
quests.correctAnswer: Rescuers are more likely to find someone who is not moving
quests.hint: The final sentence contains the reason in a compact form.
quests.explanation: A stationary group is easier for searchers to find. The options about weather and phones are twisted versions of other points.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The Everyday account has no monthly fee if at least $1,000 is deposited each month; otherwise a fee of $8 applies. Withdrawals at our own machines are free, and other banks' machines charge $2.50 each after the first three withdrawals in a month. Overdrafts up to $200 are interest-free for seven days, after which interest is charged at 18 percent. Statements are provided online, and paper statements cost $3 each. International transfers carry a flat fee of $15. Customers over sixty-five are exempt from the monthly fee, and joint accounts are available on request at no extra cost.
quests.question: What happens if an overdraft lasts ten days?
options: A flat fee of $15 is added to the account
The $8 monthly fee is charged a second time
The account is closed until the debt is repaid
Interest is charged after the seventh day
quests.correctAnswer: Interest is charged after the seventh day
quests.hint: The overdraft has a free period. Check how long ten days is compared with it.
quests.explanation: The first seven days are interest-free, so interest applies afterwards. The $15 fee is for international transfers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Our network covers 96 percent of the population with 4G, but coverage is weaker in rural areas, where it drops to 81 percent. Indoor signal may be lower than the maps show, especially in buildings with thick walls or metal roofs. In areas of poor coverage, customers can use Wi-Fi calling for free, provided their phone supports it. Roaming charges do not apply in the EU, although a fair-use limit of 20 GB a month applies to data. Customers who experience persistent problems can request a free signal booster. Maps showing planned improvements for the next two years are published on our website every spring.
quests.question: Which statement is supported by the passage?
options: Rural coverage is lower than the national figure
Boosters must be paid for
Signal is identical indoors and outdoors
Roaming in the EU has no limits at all
quests.correctAnswer: Rural coverage is lower than the national figure
quests.hint: Check each option against the exact figures and qualifiers in the passage.
quests.explanation: 81 percent in rural areas is lower than 96 percent overall. The passage warns indoor signal may differ, sets a 20 GB limit and offers boosters free.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The proposed development on the former brickworks site would include 320 homes, of which a third would be affordable, a primary school and a small park. Supporters say the site is well placed for public transport and would ease the housing shortage. Opponents worry about traffic on the single access road and the loss of habitat for bats that roost in the old chimneys. The developer has offered to fund a new junction and to install bat boxes, but the council has postponed its decision until a traffic study is completed. A public consultation will follow, with a final vote expected in the spring, and residents may register to speak at the meeting.
quests.question: Why has the council delayed its decision?
options: It is waiting for the results of a traffic study
The plans for the school changed at the last minute
The bats were discovered only recently
The developer withdrew its offer to fund a junction
quests.correctAnswer: It is waiting for the results of a traffic study
quests.hint: Ask which concern is being investigated before any decision is made.
quests.explanation: The postponement lasts until a traffic study is complete. The developer's offers are still on the table.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The language platform offers a free tier with limited lessons and adverts, a Premium plan at $12 a month and an annual Premium plan at $84. Premium removes adverts, allows offline downloads and unlocks speaking practice with a tutor, which is charged separately at $15 for a thirty-minute session. New users can try Premium for seven days at no cost, but a card must be entered, and the subscription renews automatically unless cancelled beforehand. Family plans for up to five users cost $140 a year. Discounts of thirty percent are offered each January to users who return after a lapse, but not to those on the free tier.
quests.question: How much cheaper per month is the annual plan than the monthly plan?
quests.hint: Divide the yearly price into months before comparing.
quests.explanation: $84 a year is $7 a month, which is $5 less than $12. Seven is the monthly cost of the annual plan, not the saving.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The transport smartcard costs $5 to buy, which is not refundable, and can be topped up online or at stations. Fares are capped at $8 a day and $40 a week, so passengers never pay more than that however many journeys they make. Children under sixteen travel at half price with a registered child card, and seniors travel free off-peak. If you lose the card, you must report it within twenty-four hours so that the balance can be transferred to a replacement. Cards inactive for two years expire, and any balance is lost. Tickets for special events are sold separately and are not covered by the daily or weekly caps.
quests.question: What would a passenger lose by leaving the card unused for two years?
options: Any money left on the card
The ability to top up online
The weekly fare cap
The right to a child fare
quests.correctAnswer: Any money left on the card
quests.hint: The last sentence describes the result of long inactivity.
quests.explanation: Cards that are inactive for two years expire and the balance is lost. The caps and child fares are separate features.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The city's cycling scheme has had a mixed first year. Around 4,000 bikes were placed at 200 stations, and 1.2 million journeys were made, most of them under twenty minutes. Users praised the low price of one dollar for thirty minutes, but complained that stations in the outer districts were often empty in the evenings, when bikes had been moved to the centre by earlier users. The operator has therefore begun to move bikes by van, which increases costs, and is considering a small fee for leaving bikes outside the station area. Next year it plans to add 800 bikes and 40 stations, focusing on the districts where demand exceeded supply.
quests.question: What problem is the operator trying to solve by moving bikes by van?
options: Empty stations in the outer districts in the evening
Users keeping bikes overnight without returning them
High prices for very short journeys
Bikes being stolen from stations in the centre
quests.correctAnswer: Empty stations in the outer districts in the evening
quests.hint: A connecting word links a complaint to the operator's action.
quests.explanation: Bikes gather in the centre, leaving outer stations empty, so the operator redistributes them. Price was praised, not criticised.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Travellers to the region should be aware that the rainy season runs from June to October, when roads to the mountain villages are frequently blocked by landslides. Airlines report that domestic flights are often cancelled at short notice, and it is advisable to allow at least two spare days in any itinerary. Vaccination against typhoid is recommended, and mosquito repellent is essential in lowland areas. Foreign visitors must register with the local police within seven days of arrival, and the hotel usually does this on the traveller's behalf. Bank cards are widely accepted in cities, but cash is needed in the mountains, where machines are rare and often empty.
quests.question: Why should travellers allow spare days in their itinerary?
options: Mosquitoes delay travel plans in the lowlands
Flights are often cancelled at short notice
Hotels register visitors slowly in the mountains
Vaccination against typhoid takes several days
quests.correctAnswer: Flights are often cancelled at short notice
quests.hint: The recommendation and its reason sit in the same sentence.
quests.explanation: Because domestic flights are frequently cancelled, extra days protect the plan. Registration and vaccination are separate advice.

quests.passage: Applicants for the Harlow Prize must be under thirty, hold a bachelor's degree and be planning postgraduate study in environmental science. Preference is given to those who have already done voluntary work, though this is not required. The prize of $12,000 is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on satisfactory progress reports. Applications need two references, at least one of them academic, and a statement of no more than five hundred words. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed by video in March. Successful applicants may defer their start by one year, but must confirm their acceptance within two weeks of the offer.
quests.question: Which candidate would NOT be eligible?
options: A 34-year-old graduate planning to study ecology
A 29-year-old with one academic and one employer reference
A 25-year-old with no volunteering experience
A 27-year-old applying to study environmental science
quests.correctAnswer: A 34-year-old graduate planning to study ecology
quests.hint: Check every candidate against the age rule and the required references.
quests.explanation: Only the 34-year-old breaks a firm rule, since applicants must be under thirty. Volunteering is preferred, not required, and one academic reference is enough.
